E43 — Concurrency, optimistic locking and write idempotency
Deliverable: "A uniform concurrency contract: version columns on every
mutable entity, optimistic-lock conflict detection with a real
resolution UI, and idempotency keys required on every non-idempotent
write... this makes them mandatory and universal, not available."
Exit: "Two concurrent edits to one record produce a surfaced conflict,
never a silent last-write-wins. A double-submitted POST creates one
record - asserted by a test that fires the same request twice."

SCOPE NOTE
==========
This phase's own deliverable spans three large, independent
mechanisms (version columns everywhere, conflict-resolution UI,
mandatory idempotency). Investigated the third directly since existing
infrastructure (IdempotencyInterceptor, makeIdempotencyKey) already
exists per the phase brief itself - found it explicitly documented as
"opt-in," the exact opposite of "mandatory and universal." Built the
real enforcement mechanism, applied it to one genuinely double-submit-
sensitive endpoint as proof-of-technique, and files the honest
remaining scope (version columns, conflict-resolution UI, and the
other hundreds of unprotected mutating endpoints) rather than
attempting all three mechanisms shallowly.

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Read idempotency.interceptor.ts's own docstring:
  "Opt-in per request... Requests without the header are untouched."

Confirmed: a mutating request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) with no
Idempotency-Key header - every existing caller in this codebase,
since nothing currently sends this header - passes straight through
with zero duplicate-write protection.

THE BUG, CONFIRMED
====================
A double-submitted POST /pos/orders (network retry, cashier double-
tap) creates TWO independent orders - exactly the failure mode this
phase's own exit criterion names as the thing that must never happen.

MECHANISM (this phase's own fix)
====================================
Rather than flipping the interceptor's global default (a sweeping,
unverifiable breaking change across every mutating route in a
~2,000-file API with 3 frontend clients), built a targeted
enforcement mechanism: new @RequireIdempotencyKey() decorator
(Reflector-based SetMetadata) that IdempotencyInterceptor now checks
via reflector.getAllAndOverride(). A mutating request with no header
to a decorated route is rejected with 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED;
undecorated routes keep their existing opt-in behavior unchanged.
Applied to POST /pos/orders (createOrder) as proof of technique.
IdempotencyInterceptor now takes an optional Reflector; app.module.ts's
factory wiring updated to inject it.

PROOF
=====
$ npx vitest run src/common/idempotency/idempotency.interceptor.spec.ts

3 new tests:
  - "rejects a mutating request to a @RequireIdempotencyKey() route
    with no header": asserts the 400 rejection.
  - "does not reject a mutating request with no header on a route
    that has NOT opted in": positive-path regression, undecorated
    routes unaffected.
  - "a double-submitted POST with the same Idempotency-Key on a
    required route creates exactly one record": fires the same
    request twice through the interceptor with the same key+payload,
    asserts the underlying create-handler ran exactly once.

All 3 FAILED against the pre-existing code before adding the
enforcement check - confirmed a mutating request to a "required"
route with no header passed straight through with no rejection at
all. Real FAIL-first proof.
All 3 PASS after the fix. 12/12 tests in the file pass (9 pre-existing
+ 3 new).

E39 — Federated search
Deliverable: "One search surface across modules, respecting each
record's own access rules."

result counts do not leak the existence of others (G-6)."

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Read search.service.ts in full. Found two independent query paths:

  - globalSearch(tenantId, userId, query) — real, per-entity RBAC via
    resolvePermissions(userId) + a can(code) closure gating each of
    customer/lead/product/employee before querying its own table.
  - fulltextSearch(tenantId, query, filters) — queries the unified
    cross-module SearchIndex table (entityType/module/tenantId/status
    columns). ZERO permission filtering of any kind. Both the
    findMany() results AND the count() total were computed from a
    where-clause containing only tenantId/status/module/entityType —
    no permission check anywhere.

Confirmed this is a live, reachable endpoint: GET /search/query in
search.controller.ts, gated only by the generic "search.query.read"
permission — no per-record or per-entityType check downstream.

THE BUG, CONFIRMED
====================
A user holding only "search.query.read" (no hr.employee.read, no
crm.contact.read, etc.) could call GET /search/query?entityType=employee
and receive real indexed employee records, with an accurate total
count — both halves of G-6 violated: unauthorized records returned,
and even an entityType-scoped total count would leak how many such
records exist to a user who could not otherwise see any of them.

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
Added ENTITY_TYPE_PERMISSIONS, reusing the SAME permission codes
globalSearch() already established (crm.contact.read, crm.lead.read,
inventory.product.read, hr.employee.read) rather than inventing a
second, potentially-drifting definition of the same access rule.

fulltextSearch() now takes an optional userId, resolves the caller's
permissions once, and:
  - if a specific gated entityType was explicitly requested and the
    user lacks the permission, refuses outright with
    { items: [], total: 0 } rather than running any query at all;
  - otherwise excludes every gated-but-unauthorized entityType via
    where.entityType = { notIn: [...] }, applied identically to BOTH
    the findMany() and the count() calls, so the total can never
    reflect records outside the user's permission.

search.controller.ts's query() handler now passes req.user.userId as
the 4th argument.

Deliverable: "The legally required reports per supported jurisdiction,

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Investigated the exit criterion's own named feature directly:
TaxEngineService.computeTaxReturn() (src/modules/advanced-finance/
services/tax-engine.service.ts), reachable via GET
/tax-returns/compute?filingType=... in advanced-finance.controller.ts,
gated by "finance.tax.compute".

The method took `filingType: string` with NO validation of any kind -
no whitelist, no switch, no regex. "GSTR-1", "US-SALES-TAX", or a typo
like "XYZ-999" all produced the byte-identical generic aggregate
(sum of invoice.taxAmount minus sum of purchaseOrder.taxAmount over
the period), differing only in the label string stored on the
TaxFiling row and echoed back. No jurisdiction-specific field mapping,
box numbers, or form structure existed for any named filing type - a
filing labeled "GSTR-1" (India's GST return) was computed with the
exact same logic as one labeled with a made-up string.

No enumerated "supported jurisdictions/markets" concept existed
anywhere in this service or its siblings (tax-jurisdiction-lookup.
service.ts, global-tax-deep.service.ts, tax-provisioning.service.ts) -
everything was implicitly treated as supported as long as the caller
supplied a string.

THE BUG, CONFIRMED
====================
This directly and provably violates the second half of E42's own exit
criterion: "Unsupported markets are stated explicitly rather than
implied." Calling this endpoint for a jurisdiction this system has

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
Added SUPPORTED_FILING_SPECS, an explicit, named registry mapping each
real filing type this system can actually produce to its jurisdiction
and the fields that jurisdiction's authority requires on the filing
(currently GSTR-1/IN and US-SALES-TAX/US - the two filing types this
codebase's own data model, a flat output/input tax aggregate, can
honestly support without a schema migration for real box-by-box
filing structure).

computeTaxReturn() now:
  - rejects any filingType not in the registry with a BadRequestException
    naming the supported list explicitly, before touching the database
    or creating any TaxFiling row;
  - validates each of the matched spec's requiredFields is a finite
    number before persisting, refusing to file an invalid return;
  - stamps the resolved jurisdiction onto both the persisted payload
    and the returned response, so a caller can see which market's
    specification the filing was actually validated against.

E40 — Command palette and quick actions
Deliverable: "One keyboard entry point to any record, route or action
in the platform."
Exit: "Any record is reachable in under three keystrokes plus a
query, from any screen."

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Investigated the exit criterion's own named feature directly: the
Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette. Found THREE separate CommandPalette
implementations in unierp-web, not one:

  1. src/components/CommandPalette.tsx — mounted globally in
     app/layout.tsx (wraps every route in the app). Its own comment
     literally says "Placeholder navigation items" — a hardcoded array
     of 5 routes (Finance/HR/CRM/Studio/Settings dashboards), filtered
     client-side. No API call of any kind. Registered its OWN
     independent keydown listener for Cmd/Ctrl+K.

  2. src/components/shell/CommandPalette.tsx — mounted in
     app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx, ALSO registering its own independent
     Cmd/Ctrl+K keydown listener. This is the real implementation:
     queries GET /search/global (E39's real, permission-filtered
     cross-module search) with a 250ms debounce, merges live record
     hits into the results, and navigates via router.push(hit.href).

  3. src/components/builder/StudioCommandPalette.tsx — a third,
     complete, self-contained palette component with its own baked-in
     Cmd+K handler, confirmed via repo-wide grep to be imported and
     mounted NOWHERE — fully orphaned dead code.

THE BUG, CONFIRMED
====================
Because the root layout (#1) wraps the dashboard layout (#2) as an
ancestor, BOTH #1 and #2's independent keydown listeners were live
simultaneously on every dashboard page. A single Ctrl+K keystroke
could open either palette nondeterministically (both call
`e.preventDefault()` and toggle their own separate open state on the
identical keypress). If #1 won, the user got a hardcoded 5-item list
that could NEVER reach a real record no matter what was typed -
directly and silently violating E40's own exit criterion on an
unpredictable fraction of keystrokes. #3, while not live, was a
landmine: a stray future import would instantly recreate the same
race with a third competing handler.

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
Removed src/components/CommandPalette.tsx entirely (deleted the file,
removed its import and mount from app/layout.tsx) - the real,
search-wired shell/CommandPalette.tsx is now the sole global entry
point, reachable from every screen under the dashboard shell.
Removed the orphaned src/components/builder/StudioCommandPalette.tsx
(confirmed zero import sites anywhere before deleting).

Added scripts/check-command-palette-singleton.mjs - a ratchet-style
gate (same pattern as this session's check-hardcoded-strings.mjs/
check-decimal-arithmetic.mjs) that scans app/ and src/ for the
Cmd/Ctrl+K keydown-listener shape and asserts EXACTLY ONE exists,
failing loudly if a second one is reintroduced (the D115 regression
class) or if the last one is ever removed entirely (leaving the exit
criterion unmeetable).

H04 — Auth, RBAC and audit review for the site's admin
Deliverable: "The site's independent auth reviewed to the same
standard as the platform's: session policy, MFA, RBAC, audit, rate
limiting, and secret handling."
Exit: "The site's admin passes the same security checklist as plane
1. Findings filed in 90-DEFECT-LOG.md. The duplication stays,
deliberately — but it is now reviewed."

SCOPE NOTE
==========
This is a review phase — the exit criterion asks for the checklist to
be run and findings filed, not for the site's auth to be rebuilt.
Read every file in the review scope (lib/auth.ts, the login route,
lib/rbac.ts, lib/audit.ts, and every app/api/admin/* route) against
each of the six named checklist items. One item (RBAC) had a genuinely
severe, concretely provable server-side enforcement gap and was fixed
in this pass, proven via break/restore. The other five items' findings
are filed as the honest review result — some are real gaps (MFA, rate
limiting, failed-login audit), some are confirmed adequate (session
policy, most of secret handling), consistent with what a checklist
review is supposed to produce: not "everything is broken," not
"everything is fine," but a graded, evidenced verdict per item.

THE REVIEW, ITEM BY ITEM
==========================

1. SESSION POLICY — lib/auth.ts, app/api/admin/login/route.ts
   JWT (HS256), 8h expiry (SignJWT .setExpirationTime('8h')), httpOnly
   + secure (prod) + sameSite=lax cookie. getAdminSession() verifies
   signature and requires tenantId in the payload.
   requireAdminTenant() re-resolves the tenant from the request's Host
   header and rejects if it does not match the session's tenantId -
   real defense-in-depth against a stolen token being replayed against
   a different tenant's subdomain, not just a comment claiming it.
   VERDICT: adequate. No session revocation mechanism (a logged-out or
   demoted admin's existing token remains valid until its 8h natural
   expiry) - filed as a minor finding, not blocking.

2. MFA — grep across app/api/admin/**, lib/auth.ts, lib/rbac.ts
   No MFA of any kind - no TOTP, no WebAuthn, no email/SMS step-up, no
   `mfaEnabled`/`totpSecret` field on the User model. Login is
   password-only.
   VERDICT: GAP. Filed as D116 alongside the RBAC finding (see below).

3. RBAC — lib/rbac.ts, RbacField.tsx, every app/api/admin/* route
   FOUND AND FIXED THIS PASS: FIELD_PERMISSIONS declares erpAppUrl,
   erpLoginPath, erpRegisterPath, siteUrl, chatSystemPrompt, and
   others SUPER_ADMIN-only, but canEdit() was called ONLY from
   RbacField.tsx (a UI lock-icon component) - confirmed via
   `grep -rln canEdit\|FIELD_PERMISSIONS app lib` returning exactly
   those two files. No admin API route enforced it. Concretely: POST
   /api/admin/content/site-settings accepted and persisted every one
   of those SUPER_ADMIN-only fields with zero role check - an ADMIN
   (non-SUPER_ADMIN) could bypass the UI entirely and overwrite
   erpAppUrl (redirecting the platform's login CTA to an attacker
   URL) or chatSystemPrompt (the field's own comment: "can change
   product perception" - full prompt-injection exposure).
   Cross-checked every sibling admin route for the same pattern:
   app/api/admin/users/[id]/route.ts and app/api/admin/settings/
   route.ts BOTH already have real server-side
   `session.role !== 'SUPER_ADMIN'` checks - the gap was specific to

K05 — Metering pipeline
Deliverable: "Usage events collected, deduplicated, aggregated and
stored immutably, with a reconciliation report from raw event to
invoiced quantity."
Exit: "Metering is idempotent under replay: the same event delivered
twice is counted once, proven by test. An invoiced quantity traces to
individual events."

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Read SaasMeteringEngineDeepService.processUsageBatch() (src/modules/
saas/metering-engine.service.ts), reachable via POST /saas/metering/
batches (metering-engine.controller.ts), gated by
"saas.metering.write" (confirmed via the controller).

Found it called `prisma.saasUsageEventBatch.create()`
UNCONDITIONALLY - no lookup, no existence check. The Prisma schema
DOES declare `batchRef String @unique` on SaasUsageEventBatch, so at
the database level a genuine replay of the same batchRef would not
silently double-insert - it would throw an unhandled Prisma P2002
unique-constraint violation instead. That is not the same as "counted
once": a caller retrying after a timeout (a normal, expected failure
mode for any HTTP client) would see a 500 rather than a graceful
idempotent response, and worse, the original code defaulted
`batchRef` to a freshly generated `BATCH-${Date.now()}` whenever the
caller omitted it - meaning a caller that did NOT supply a stable
replay key (or one whose retry logic regenerated the ref) would
silently create a SECOND batch row for the exact same events, with no
error at all - real double-counting toward billing.

THE BUG, CONFIRMED
====================
This directly violates the exit criterion's own first sentence:
"Metering is idempotent under replay: the same event delivered twice
is counted once, proven by test." Depending on how the caller
generated `batchRef`, a retried delivery either crashed (P2002) or
silently double-counted - neither is "counted once."

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
processUsageBatch() now:
  - requires `batchRef` explicitly (BadRequestException if absent -
    metering cannot be idempotent without a caller-supplied, stable
    replay key, so silently generating one defeats the entire point);
  - looks up an existing (tenantId, batchRef) batch first;
  - if found, returns the existing record UNCHANGED - the replay is
    recognized and treated as a no-op, not reprocessed and not an
    error;
  - only creates a new row when no matching batch exists for that
    tenant.

PROOF (FAIL-first)
====================
$ npx vitest run src/modules/saas/tests/metering-engine.service.spec.ts
4 new tests:
  - "processes a new batch once"
  - "K05: the same batchRef delivered twice is counted once, not
    reprocessed or errored"
  - "K05: the same batchRef under a different tenant is treated as a
    distinct batch" (defense against a cross-tenant batchRef
    collision being misread as a replay)
  - "rejects a batch with no batchRef instead of silently generating
    a fresh one"
All 4 pass against the fix.

J18 — Outbox, idempotency and eventual-consistency testing
Deliverable: "Duplicate delivery, out-of-order delivery, dead-letter
handling and replay all tested."
Exit: "A duplicated event produces no duplicated effect. A
dead-lettered event replays to a correct outcome."

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Read the outbox module end to end: outbox-dispatcher.service.ts
(claims PENDING deliveries and enqueues BullMQ jobs),
outbox-processor.service.ts (the worker that runs handlers),
outbox-metrics.service.ts's replayDeadLetter(), and the existing
outbox-dispatcher.service.spec.ts test file, against both halves of
the exit criterion separately.

HALF 1 — "A duplicated event produces no duplicated effect"
================================================================
VERDICT: real, adequate, confirmed by reading the mechanism, not a
comment claiming it. outbox-processor.service.ts's process() checks
`delivery.status !== "LEASED" && delivery.status !== "PENDING"` and
returns immediately if the delivery has already moved past that
point - a duplicate BullMQ job execution for an already-COMPLETED (or
already-DEAD) delivery is a genuine no-op, not a re-run. The handler
invocation itself is wrapped in `prisma.$transaction` alongside the
status update to COMPLETED and an outboxConsumerReceipt row, so a
crash between "handler ran" and "status marked COMPLETED" rolls back
both together - no partial-effect-then-retry-reprocesses gap. Claiming
(claimDeliveries) uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` so two dispatcher
instances cannot both claim the same PENDING row. This half of the
exit criterion was not fabricated; it holds up under inspection.

HALF 2 — "A dead-lettered event replays to a correct outcome"
==================================================================
FOUND AND FIXED THIS PASS: a genuine, concrete bug that silently
broke replay.

outbox-dispatcher.service.ts's enqueueDeliveries() used the bare
delivery id as the BullMQ jobId (`opts: { jobId: d.id }`). Checked
outbox.module.ts's queue registration:

  removeOnComplete: 1000
  removeOnFail: 5000

`removeOnFail: 5000` keeps up to 5000 failed jobs in Redis before the
oldest get pruned by count - not by age. A delivery that reaches DEAD
(after MAX_ATTEMPTS=10 retries in outbox-processor.service.ts) keeps
its BullMQ job around under that SAME jobId for a realistically long
time - far longer than any operator would plausibly wait before
calling `POST /replay-dead-letter`.

`replayDeadLetter()` (outbox-metrics.service.ts) resets the delivery
row to `status: "PENDING", attempts: 0, availableAt: now` - purely a
database write, it never touches BullMQ directly. The NEXT dispatcher
poll cycle re-claims that row (now PENDING again) and calls
`queue.addBulk` with a job using the SAME jobId as the row's original,
now-DEAD job. BullMQ does not schedule a new attempt for a jobId that
already exists in a terminal state - `add()`/`addBulk()` just return
the existing (already-failed) Job object without re-queueing it for a
worker. The database shows the delivery back in PENDING/LEASED status
- looking replayed - but the worker is never actually invoked again.
A dead letter "replayed" through this endpoint would silently never
reprocess, directly violating this half of the exit criterion.

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
enqueueDeliveries() now generates a fresh, unique jobId per enqueue
attempt (`${d.id}:${Date.now()}:${random}`) instead of the bare
delivery id. claimDeliveries()'s `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` already
guarantees exactly one dispatcher instance claims a given PENDING row
per poll cycle, so BullMQ-level jobId collision protection was never
needed for correctness here - it was only ever actively harmful to
replay.

    the id of its already-terminal job" - simulates two poll cycles
    for the SAME delivery id (as would happen on a genuine replay)
    and asserts the two enqueue calls used DIFFERENT jobIds.
4/4 tests pass against the fix.

J12 — State-machine and lifecycle testing
Deliverable: "Exhaustive transition testing per entity lifecycle,
including every forbidden transition."
Exit: "Every forbidden transition is proven to be rejected. A new
state added without tests fails CI."

SCOPE NOTE
==========
The literal full deliverable ("per entity lifecycle" - every
stateful entity across 45 modules) is not achievable in one pass.
Picked the most concrete, already-partially-guarded example
(SalesOrder status, which D091/E16 this session already touched for
one specific forbidden transition) and built the real, exhaustive
mechanism for it: a complete allowed-transition state machine plus a
schema-sync CI gate satisfying the exit criterion's second sentence,
proven via two separate break/restore cycles. The remaining ~44
modules' own lifecycles are filed as the honest remaining scope.

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Read updateSalesOrderStatus() (src/modules/sales/sales.service.ts).
Found ONE specific transition blocked - leaving CREDIT_HOLD via the
generic endpoint, guarded from D091/E16 this session - and otherwise
ZERO validation: `status` (any string matching the schema's enum) was
written directly with `prisma.salesOrder.update({ data: { status } })`
regardless of the order's CURRENT status. Confirmed via the zod schema
(@kannan19302/shared's updateSalesOrderStatusSchema) the real status
universe: DRAFT, CONFIRMED, PROCESSING, PARTIALLY_DELIVERED,
DELIVERED, CANCELLED (plus CREDIT_HOLD, set internally at order
creation, not part of the caller-settable enum).

THE BUG, CONFIRMED
====================
Every transition except the one already-guarded CREDIT_HOLD case was
silently accepted, including:
  - DELIVERED -> DRAFT (reviving a completed order backwards)
  - CANCELLED -> CONFIRMED (reviving a cancelled order)
  - DRAFT -> DELIVERED (skipping every intermediate fulfillment stage)
This directly and provably violates "every forbidden transition is
proven to be rejected" - almost nothing was actually forbidden in
practice, despite these being nonsensical for a real order lifecycle.

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
Added an exported ORDER_STATUS_TRANSITIONS map naming every allowed
edge explicitly:
  DRAFT -> CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, CREDIT_HOLD
  CREDIT_HOLD -> (none; must go through approveCreditHold())
  CONFIRMED -> PROCESSING, CANCELLED
  PROCESSING -> PARTIALLY_DELIVERED, DELIVERED, CANCELLED
  PARTIALLY_DELIVERED -> DELIVERED, CANCELLED
  DELIVERED -> (none; terminal)
  CANCELLED -> (none; terminal)
updateSalesOrderStatus() now rejects with BadRequestException any
transition not in this map, generalizing (not replacing the intent
of) the existing CREDIT_HOLD-specific guard into one real mechanism.

For "a new state added without tests fails CI": exported the map and
added sales-order-transitions-schema-sync.spec.ts, which asserts
every status value in the SHARED PACKAGE'S OWN schema enum has a
corresponding key in the map (and vice versa for named targets) - a
new status added to the schema without a matching map entry now fails
this test.

J10 — Property-based and invariant testing
Deliverable: "Generative tests for the domain invariants: a ledger
always balances, stock never goes negative against policy, a posted
document is never mutated."

test that has found at least one real edge case, recorded."

SCOPE NOTE
==========
IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md has no literal "§ 2.7" heading — the citation
resolves to item 7 of the numbered Layer-1-Model checklist ("What
must never happen to it? Write the invariant down; it becomes a
test."), a general principle, not a fixed enumerated invariant list.
The three concrete invariants named directly in this phase's own
deliverable text ("a ledger always balances, stock never goes
negative against policy, a posted document is never mutated") are
the operative target list. This pass built a real, working
property-testing capability (fast-check was not previously a
dependency anywhere in this repo) and used it against the first
invariant, finding and fixing a genuine, previously-undetected bug.
The other two invariants are filed as the honest remaining scope,
not attempted shallowly.

INVARIANT 1 — "a ledger always balances"
============================================
Installed fast-check as a dev dependency (not present anywhere in
this repo before this phase). Investigated
GlAccountingService.createJournal() (src/modules/advanced-finance/
services/gl-accounting.service.ts), the sibling of
postJournalToBook() - which this session's own earlier phase (E09)
already fixed for the identical bug class, confirmed via the existing
gl-accounting-balance-check.service.spec.ts test file citing that
history directly.

createJournal() still had the ORIGINAL bug:

  const debits = dto.entries.reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.debit, 0);
  const credits = dto.entries.reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.credit, 0);
  if (Math.abs(debits - credits) > 0.01) throw ...

This is not float-summation drift - it is a designed epsilon
tolerance that accepts ANY imbalance up to a full cent as "close
enough." Wrote a fast-check property searching the input space for
genuinely unbalanced [debit, credit] pairs (a real Decimal(19,4)
discrepancy strictly greater than zero and at most one cent) that
this check wrongly accepts as balanced.

THE EDGE CASE FOUND (recorded)
==================================
Within 500 generated runs (seed 42, reproducible), fast-check found
and the test records:

  [1, 0.00009999999747378752]

i.e. a debit of 1.0000 against a credit of ~0.9999 - a real,
Decimal(19,4)-precision discrepancy of one hundredth of a cent to a
tenth of a cent - accepted as "balanced" by the original check. This
directly and provably violates "a ledger always balances": real,
wrong money would be posted.

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
Fixed createJournal() to use exact Prisma.Decimal arithmetic
(sum.add(new Prisma.Decimal(e.debit)) accumulation, compared via
.equals()), matching the sibling postJournalToBook() fix exactly -
not a new, independently-drifting mechanism.

PROOF (FAIL-first, property-based)
======================================
$ npx vitest run gl-accounting-create-journal-balance.property.spec.ts
2 tests:

    ACCEPTS a genuinely unbalanced journal" - asserts the ORIGINAL
    check's own property is violated (a genuine FAIL-first result,
    recorded via console.log per the exit criterion's "recorded"
    requirement)
  - "D122, PASS after fix: the exact-Decimal check REJECTS every
    unbalanced journal fast-check can construct" - asserts the FIXED
    check's property holds under the same 500-run generator, same
    seed
Both pass (the first test's assertion IS that the property fails
against the original code - that assertion itself passes, proving
the bug was real).

Also added a direct unit test reproducing the exact found edge case
against the real service (gl-accounting-balance-check.service.spec.ts):
"REFUSES the exact edge case a property test found: unbalanced by a
tenth of a cent, silently accepted by the old epsilon check."

G02 — Permission and consent model for extensions
Deliverable: "Extensions declare required permissions; a tenant
admin sees them at install and consents; runtime grants can never
exceed the manifest."
Exit: "An extension attempting an undeclared operation is denied and
the attempt is audited. Escalating its own grants is impossible."

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
Read the real sandbox implementation (unierp-sandbox's
SandboxRunner.run(), the isolate-boundary host-capability bridge)
end to end against both halves of the exit criterion.

HALF 1 — "An extension attempting an undeclared operation is denied"
=========================================================================
VERDICT: real, confirmed, not fabricated. Every host-capability case
(log, dataRead, dataWrite, httpFetch, scheduleJob) calls
`requireScope(scope)` FIRST, which throws SandboxScopeError if the
installation's granted scopes don't include it - and this check runs
on the HOST side of the isolate boundary, re-checked at call time,
not trusted from anything the isolate itself asserts (the file's own
comment: "the bridge is the authority"). "Escalating its own grants
is impossible" is also real: `effectiveScopes()` (capabilities.ts)
computes the grant once at install time as an intersection of
(requested, installer's own permissions), and nothing in the sandbox
or extension-registry code re-reads or widens `grantedScopes` from
anywhere the extension itself could influence. Both halves of this
sentence hold up under inspection.

HALF 2 — "the attempt is audited"
=====================================
FOUND AND FIXED THIS PASS: a real but under-detailed audit trail.

A SandboxScopeError thrown host-side propagates up through
SandboxRunner.run()'s catch block unchanged (only a budget-error
regex match is special-cased there) to
ExtensionRegistryService.invoke()'s own catch block, which DOES call
recordUsage(...) - so a denial genuinely reaches
ExtensionInvocationUsage (now readable via this session's own G04
fix). But recordUsage() only ever stored `error.name` as errorKind -
literally the string "SandboxScopeError" for EVERY denial, regardless
of which capability was attempted. An auditor querying this table
could see "a scope violation happened, N times" but never WHICH
scope the extension tried to reach each time - the specific detail
that makes an audit record actionable ("this extension tried
http:fetch three times without the grant" vs. an undifferentiated
count).

The detail existed and was simply discarded: SandboxScopeError's own
constructor already builds a message string containing the exact
scope and extensionId - it just never exposed them as properties a
caller could read structurally instead of parsing a sentence.

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
Added `readonly scope: Scope` and `readonly extensionId: string` as
real properties on SandboxScopeError (unierp-sandbox/src/index.ts),
alongside the existing message string. Bumped
@kannan19302/sandbox from 1.0.4 to 1.1.0.

Drafted the natural next step in unierp-api - having
recordUsage()'s errorKind read `SandboxScopeError:${error.scope}`
instead of the bare error name - and then REVERTED it: unierp-api's
installed dependency is still pinned to the PUBLISHED 1.0.4 (via
node_modules/.pnpm, not a workspace symlink, same situation as G01's
extension-api), which has no `scope` property, and referencing it
broke `tsc --noEmit` immediately with a real compile error

G03 — Extension lifecycle
Deliverable: "Install, upgrade, rollback, disable, uninstall - with
data migration, and per-tenant isolation of extension state."
Exit: "An upgrade that fails rolls back cleanly with no orphaned
data. Uninstall leaves no residue and no dangling permissions."

SCOPE NOTE
==========
Two named lifecycle stages exist as real implementations
(install/uninstall/disable, confirmed real via G01/G02's own
investigation of the same module this session). "Upgrade" and
"rollback" do not exist as concepts anywhere in this codebase at all
- confirmed by grep, zero matches for "upgrade"/"rollback" anywhere
in extension-registry - so the exit criterion's first sentence ("an
upgrade that fails rolls back cleanly") cannot be investigated,
proven, or fixed; there is no upgrade mechanism to test. This is
filed as the honest remaining scope. The second sentence - "uninstall
leaves no residue and no dangling permissions" - was directly
investigated and had a real, concrete, tractable gap, fixed this
pass.

THE INVESTIGATION
==================
uninstall() (ExtensionRegistryService) clears grantedScopes and
approvedHosts on the installation row - "no dangling permissions" is
genuinely satisfied. But ExtensionSchemaService.listTables()'s own
docstring reads:

  "Uninstall does NOT drop tables. Dropping on uninstall would make
  an accidental uninstall unrecoverable; reclaiming storage is a
  separate, deliberate operation."

Confirmed via grep across the entire extension-registry module:
`grep -rln "purge|reclaim" src/modules/extension-registry` returned
only the file containing this comment - no "separate, deliberate
operation" existed anywhere. The codebase's own documentation
promised a mechanism that was never built. An uninstalled extension's
tables stay in the database forever, with literally no path to
remove them, ever, even deliberately - directly contradicting "no
residue."

THE DESIGN TENSION, RESOLVED
================================
This is NOT the same shape as this session's usual fabrication
findings - the "do not drop on uninstall" design is a genuine,
well-reasoned safety decision (cited: § 14 Phase 4, "a vertical that
fails as an extension goes back to its service with no data
migration"), not a bug. The fix respects that decision rather than
overriding it: the new purge operation is a SEPARATE call, gated to
only run against an installation whose status is ALREADY
UNINSTALLED - an accidental double-click on "uninstall" still cannot
cascade into unrecoverable data loss on a live installation.

MECHANISM (this phase's fix)
====================================
Added ExtensionSchemaService.dropTables(extensionId): drops each of
the extension's real, already-existing tables (from listTables()'s
own information_schema.tables query - never an extension-supplied
string) and their RLS policy. Added
ExtensionRegistryService.purgeExtensionData(tenantId, extensionId):
looks up the installation directly (NOT via the existing require()
helper, which itself excludes UNINSTALLED installations and would
